LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.DeliverItemsViaDro: Enabling this option allows the orbital trader to deliver items to your colony via drop pod like in vanilla, rather than sending a shuttle that drops them off.\n\nNOTE: The setting's value is applied to a trade agreement upon initiation. Therefore, altering this value won't impact ongoing trades; it will take effect only when you initiate your next trade.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.UseMinimumTradeThr: Does it really make sense for an orbital trader and their crew to spend the time, fuel and energy it takes to send down two shuttles all for the sake of a single, cheap trade item? Enabling this and setting a threshold value below makes it so the traders won't accept trades that involves an exchange worth less than the threshold.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.HitPointsTolerance: When a traded item's condition (hit points) affects its price, the shuttle normally requires the hauled item to still be in (almost) the exact condition it was in when the deal was struck. This setting allows the item's hit points to drift by up to this percentage of its maximum (or 5 hit points, whichever is larger) and still count as a match, so minor deterioration doesn't get a trade stuck.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.MinimumTradeVariat: For each trader, a random value up to {0}% of the baseline is calculated and either added to or subtracted from the baseline threshold to give the threshold some variation.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.MultiItemShuttleLo: Lets colonists carry several stacks of goods at once when loading a trade shuttle instead of hauling one stack per trip, which speeds up loading large trades considerably, much like how the mod Pick Up And Haul works for other kinds of hauling. Turning it off returns vanilla's shuttle-loading code, which loads a single stack of items at a time.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.ActiveTradePausesD: Active trade agreement pauses trade ship departure timer

By default (when this option is not enabled), the departure timer for the orbital trader continues ticking even during an active trade. However, when this option is enabled, an active trade pauses the timer, allowing you to take all the time you need to complete your trades.\n\nNOTE: The setting's value is applied to a trade agreement upon initiation. Therefore, altering this value won't impact ongoing trades; it will take effect only when you initiate your next trade.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.NoEffectWhenActive: The settings below have no effect when the "Active trade agreement pauses trade ship departure timer" setting is enabled.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.MinTimeUntilDepart: Minimum time until departure before adding grace time: {0} hours

If a trade is made when there is less time left before an orbital trader leaves than this setting, the orbital trader will extend their stay with an additional amount of time configurable below. For the sake of balance, the orbital trader will still stop accepting new trades once the original departure time is reached.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.DepartureGraceTime: Grace time added if below minimum time: {0} hours

If a trade is made when there is less time left before an orbital trader leaves than the amount of time configurable above, the orbital trader will extend their stay with this additional amount of time. For the sake of balance, the orbital trader will still stop accepting new trades once the original departure time is reached.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.BuyMoreTimeHoursLa: Time added per "Buy more time" purchase: {0} hours
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.BuyMoreTimeHoursTo: How much extra time is added to a trade shuttle's departure timer each time you pay to buy more time.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.BuyMoreTimeBaseCos: The silver cost of the first "Buy more time" purchase for a given trade shuttle.
LanguageData.RealisticOrbitalTrade.BuyMoreTimeCostGro: "Buy more time" cost growth per purchase: x{0}
Each additional "Buy more time" purchase for the same trade shuttle multiplies the silver cost by this amount, so stalling a shuttle indefinitely gets increasingly expensive.
